The Next Biopharma Revolution: Quantum Computing

Pharmaceutical Executive October 28, 2026
Sam Anwar

Key Takeaways

  • Vendor roadmaps increasingly converge on fault-tolerant quantum computing around 2029–2030, while near-term value is expected via hybrid quantum–classical pilots in early discovery through 2028.
  • Quantum computing is framed as complementary to AI, with AI extracting insights and automating decisions while quantum targets computational bottlenecks in chemistry, simulation, and optimization.
  • High-impact use cases include accurate ligand–target modeling, metalloenzyme chemistry, protein conformational dynamics, adaptive trial optimization, and large-scale genetic interaction analysis.
  • Readiness priorities emphasize inventorying data assets, consolidating onto modern clinical data platforms, strengthening metadata/lineage, designing for hybrid compute portability, and extending AI governance frameworks to quantum.
